context.requirement_text:
Third and final part of ISS-0431/GH#835's fix, covering its own
explicitly-named SECONDARY surface: "Poller's per-tenant sweeps and
future LISTEN/NOTIFY work (ISS-0430) are secondary surfaces to cover
by the same decision rather than each inventing its own cap." Atop
REQ-216's core module; does not touch REQ-217's HTTP-path wiring.

WHAT `lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex` ACTUALLY DOES TODAY (read in
full, not assumed): `handle_info(:tick, ...)` calls
`Enum.each(schemas, fn schema_name -> Scheduler.poll_and_fire(schema_name)
end)` -- SEQUENTIAL, one tenant schema at a time, not concurrent. The
same sequential pattern repeats for
`maybe_run_retention_sweep/2`, `maybe_run_alert_detection/3`,
`maybe_run_ordering_cycle/1`, `maybe_run_ordering_sweeper/1`,
`maybe_run_ordering_metrics/1`. So THIS module does not exhibit
unbounded CONCURRENT demand the way the HTTP path does (each call
blocks the single Poller GenServer process, so at most one DB
connection is held by Poller work at any instant) -- the real gap
here is ACCOUNTING, not concurrency: Poller's one held connection is
invisible to REQ-216's admission budget, so REQ-216's global cap
(`pool_size - reserved_headroom`) can only be a safe ceiling on
HTTP-path concurrency if `reserved_headroom` already reserves enough
slack for Poller's own use -- an implicit, untested assumption today.
This requirement makes that assumption explicit and enforced rather
than merely documented.

SCOPE:
1. Before each of the six sequential per-tenant operations named
above (the timer poll-and-fire loop plus the five `maybe_run_*`
sweeps), acquire ONE global admission slot via
`Letflow.Admission.try_acquire(:global)` for that operation's single
Repo-touching call, and release it immediately after that call
returns (success or the operation's own already-established rescue
path -- do not weaken any existing per-operation try/rescue
isolation boundary documented in poller.ex's moduledoc, e.g.
`maybe_run_alert_detection/3`'s own `rescue _ -> :ok`; the
acquire/release wraps around the existing isolation, it does not
replace it).
2. On `{:error, :capacity}` from `try_acquire(:global)` for a given
schema's operation within a tick: skip that one schema's operation
for that tick only (do not crash the GenServer, do not skip every
other schema's turn, do not skip that schema's OTHER operations this
tick if a later `try_acquire` call for a different operation
succeeds) -- mirroring `fetch_tenant_schemas/0`'s own existing
per-tick-degrades-gracefully philosophy already documented in this
module's moduledoc, applied per-schema-per-operation rather than
per-tick.
3. Poller does NOT use REQ-216's per-tenant semaphore -- only
`:global`. Reasoning: Poller's sweep already iterates every tenant
schema once per tick by design (REQ-186's own decision), so a
per-tenant CAP on Poller would not bound fairness between tenants the
way it does for bursty HTTP traffic, it would only cause a tenant to
be silently skipped some ticks for no client-visible reason -- a
strictly worse outcome for a background sweep whose whole contract is
"every tenant gets a turn." Stated explicitly rather than left
implicit.
4. No change to `Letflow.Application`'s supervision tree (no new
process; Poller remains the sole caller, same GenServer, same child
entry) and no change to `Letflow.Scheduler`'s own `poll_and_fire/1`
contract (unchanged input/output; the acquire/release wraps its call
site in `poller.ex`, per §1 above).
NOT IN THIS REQUIREMENT: no change to REQ-216's core semaphore or
REQ-217's HTTP-path wiring; no change to ISS-0430's future LISTEN/
NOTIFY work (named by ISS-0431 as a future secondary surface to cover
"by the same decision," not this requirement's own job to build); no
change to any `maybe_run_*` function's own internal per-schema
rescue logic beyond wrapping it in acquire/release.

task.description: WF-02 Step 3: independently verify test-coverage completeness for REQ-218's 6 acceptance criteria against ELIXIR-DEV's existing 6-describe-block suite (test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs), paying particular attention to AC1's mock/spy-wording substitution, AC3's two independent sub-clauses, the after-based release surviving the rescue path (not just the happy path), and global-only enforcement being asserted by a real test rather than an informal grep. Add any genuine gap found. Write test/specs/REQ-218.md. Run mix letflow.check.test and quote real output.
acceptance_criteria: with REQ-216's global cap artificially forced to 0 (test config override), a tick over 3 tenant schemas calls Scheduler.poll_and_fire/1 ZERO times for any of them (each skipped for capacity), the GenServer does not crash, and the next tick (cap restored) resumes normally -- verified by a test asserting the mock/spy call count is exactly 0 during the forced-zero tick and exactly 3 on the following tick

with the global cap forced to admit exactly 1 concurrent unit, a tick still processes all 3 tenant schemas' timer poll-and-fire loop to completion (sequential acquire/release, not a permanent block), confirmed by observing all 3 schemas' poll_and_fire/1 calls occur within that single tick

an admission {:error, :capacity} for one schema's operation within a tick does not prevent a DIFFERENT schema's SAME operation, or that SAME schema's OTHER operations, from being attempted later in the same tick -- explicit test forcing capacity exhaustion mid-tick and observing partial, not total, skip

Letflow.Admission.try_acquire({:tenant, _}) is never called anywhere in lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex -- grep-verified, confirming decision 3's per-tenant-exclusion is actually implemented, not just described

an existing per-operation rescue path (e.g. maybe_run_alert_detection/3's rescue _ -> :ok) still catches its own operation's raise with the new acquire/release wrapped around it -- a test forcing that operation to raise still leaves the admission slot released (no leak) and the tick completes
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted

result.summary:
Read docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-218 entry directly for the authoritative 6-criterion acceptance_criteria list (not paraphrased from any handoff), plus step-00/step-02/step-03 handoffs, lib/letflow/design/req218-poller-admission-wiring.md in full, lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex in full, and test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs in full (12 existing tests across 6 REQ-218 describe blocks plus pre-existing REQ-186/188/ISS-0429 blocks).

AC-TO-TEST MAPPING TABLE (also written to test/specs/REQ-218.md):

AC1 (global cap forced to 0, zero poll_and_fire calls, no crash, next tick resumes) -> describe "REQ-218 AC1: forced-zero admission cap skips every schema; capacity restored resumes normally", 1 test. Letflow.Admission.init/1 floors global_cap at max(pool_size - reserved_headroom, 1) -- literal 0 is unreachable -- so the test drives global_cap == 1 and holds the sole unit via a probe try_acquire(:global) BEFORE the tick, guaranteeing every admission attempt that tick observes exhaustion. Mock/spy substitution verified sound: this codebase has no mocking library (confirmed via mix.exs); the design doc's own §7 Q3 explicitly flags this wording conflict and directs substituting a real-effect assertion. The test asserts 3 schemas' due timers stay "pending" while the probe is held (equivalent to a spy call-count of 0, since poll_and_fire/1's only externally observable effect for a due timer IS that status transition), then all 3 fire on a second tick after release.
AC2 (cap of 1 still drains all schemas within one tick) -> describe "REQ-218 AC2...", 1 test: global_cap == 1, no probe held, 3 schemas' due timers all fire within one tick.
AC3 (two independent sub-clauses -- GAP FOUND, see below) -> (a) different-schema-same-operation: describe "REQ-218 AC3: a capacity rejection...", 1 test (ELIXIR-DEV's original, unchanged): a continuously-looping antagonist Task contends against 10 schemas' own poll_and_fire attempts, retried up to 5 times until a genuine partial skip is observed. (b) same-schema-other-operations: describe "REQ-218 AC3 (per-schema clause)...", 1 test -- NEWLY ADDED this step, see gap-check below.
AC4 ({:tenant,_} never called, grep-verified) -> describe "REQ-218 AC4...", 1 test: reads the actual poller.ex source text and asserts no "{:tenant," substring anywhere -- a real, automated ExUnit assertion (not an informal grep quoted in a handoff), matching this file's own pre-existing "no second ticker" test's precedent (grepping for `use GenServer`). Confirmed this satisfies the project's own convention of encoding such invariants as executable checks, not just described ones.
AC5 (rescue still catches, no leak) -> describe "REQ-218 AC5...", 1 test: drops only the effect_completions table from an otherwise-intact schema (surgical fault injection, avoids a separate pre-existing poll_and_fire/1 raise-safety gap already flagged and out-of-scope per ELIXIR-DEV/REVIEWER), forces maybe_run_ordering_cycle/1's rescue to catch a real raise, confirms a DIFFERENT schema's own timer still fires (no total-tick poisoning), and confirms a post-tick try_acquire(:global) still succeeds under global_cap == 1 (proving the after clause released the raised call's ref, not leaked). Confirmed this genuinely exercises the after-based release surviving the RESCUE path specifically (not just the happy path) -- a test that only ever forced the happy path would leave the after clause's actual reason for existing (belt-and-suspenders past rows 3-6's own rescue, and the ONLY release mechanism for rows 1-2 which have no inner rescue) unverified.
AC6 (mix test / mix compile --warnings-as-errors pass) -> verified by direct command runs, see below.

GAP FOUND AND FIXED: AC3's requirement text names TWO independent sub-clauses -- "a DIFFERENT schema's SAME operation" and "that SAME schema's OTHER operations" -- but the existing AC3 test only exercised the first (10 schemas racing an antagonist for the same poll_and_fire operation). A coarser, explicitly-forbidden design (one acquire/release per SCHEMA covering all six of its operations at once, ruled out by the design doc's own §1/§3) would still have passed every assertion in that existing test, since it never looks at more than one operation per schema -- meaning the existing suite did not actually distinguish the shipped per-operation-call design from that forbidden coarser one. Added describe "REQ-218 AC3 (per-schema clause): a rejected schema's other ops still proceed" (1 new test) to close this.

THREE REAL BUGS FOUND AND FIXED WHILE BUILDING THE NEW TEST (full account in test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs's own in-file comments on ac3b_attempt/3 and clear_pending_events!/1):
1. First draft used a two-sided continuous-antagonist race (mirroring AC3(a)'s own pattern, contending against BOTH the target schema's poll_and_fire AND its retention-sweep admission calls at once). This passed in isolated re-runs but failed once in a full mix letflow.check.test run (see verification below) -- root-caused via temporary IO.puts diagnostic instrumentation (since removed): with a sole global unit and a tight-looping antagonist, BOTH of the target's admission attempts overwhelmingly land on the SAME side of the race together far more often than they split (observed multiple full 60-attempt runs where EVERY attempt was false/false) -- a structurally biased design, not merely occasionally flaky, that no amount of added retries would reliably fix.
2. A related bug in that same first draft: a rejected attempt's own seeded (retention-eligible) event stayed pending and got swept up together with a LATER attempt's own event once that later attempt's retention admission succeeded, inflating that later attempt's own archived-count delta past the expected +1 and producing a false negative independent of the actual admission outcome. Fixed via a new clear_pending_events!/1 helper called at the start of every attempt.
3. Replaced the two-sided race entirely with a largely-deterministic design: the TEST process itself holds the sole global unit BEFORE handle_info/2 is even invoked, so the tick's very first admission attempt (this schema's poll_and_fire, with strictly nothing else that could have taken or released the unit first -- same-process happens-before ordering) is deterministically rejected, with NO race on that side at all. A short-lived helper Task then releases the unit after a fixed 5ms delay, leaving only ONE race (whether release beats the schema's own later retention-sweep admission attempt) -- 12 filler schemas (provisioned once, reused across up to 10 retries) widen the real elapsed DB round-trip time between the target's two admission attempts enough for the fixed delay to reliably land in between. Verified empirically: 0ms and 1ms release delays broke the FIRST (poll-rejected) guarantee outright (release raced ahead of poll's own attempt); 5ms with no filler schemas left the window too narrow for the SECOND (retention-succeeds) side to reliably land inside it; 5ms + 12 filler schemas passed 20/20 consecutive isolated runs and 3/3 consecutive full-file runs (13/13 each).

COMMANDS RUN, ALL IN THE FOREGROUND WITH REAL OUTPUT (this agent is a subagent and does not receive background-task notifications -- every long-running command was polled to completion by checking its PID directly, per the coordinator's own correction mid-task):
1. `mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force` -- 'Compiling 186 files (.ex)' / 'Generated letflow app', zero warnings, zero errors (run repeatedly across each design iteration of the new test).
2. `mix test test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs --only describe:"REQ-218 AC3 (per-schema clause)..."` (isolated) -- run 20 consecutive times against the FINAL design: 20/20 passed, 0 failures.
3. `mix test test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs` (full file) -- run 3 consecutive times against the final design: 'Result: 13 passed' each time (39.3-41.0s each), 0 failures.
4. `mix letflow.check.test` (full suite) -- run TWICE. First run (against the pre-fix, two-sided-race draft of the new test): 'Result: 3138/3141 passed (6/6 properties, 3132/3135 tests), 21 excluded', 3 failed -- 2 were the pre-existing, environment-only Mix.Tasks.Letflow.CheckToolchainTest "rust pin (REQ-165)" failures (this host has no rustc on PATH, confirmed directly, identical to the gap already documented in test/specs/REQ-217.md), the 3rd was the new AC3(b) test itself (the flake root-caused and fixed per bug 1 above). Second run, after the fix: 'Finished in 1667.1 seconds (13.9s async, 1653.1s sync)' / 'Result: 3139/3141 passed (6/6 properties, 3133/3135 tests), 21 excluded' / 'Failed: 2 tests' -- both remaining failures confirmed by name to be the same 2 pre-existing rustc-toolchain tests, ZERO REQ-218 test failures. The target ISS-0069 substring ("default values for the optional arguments") occurs zero times in this run's captured output (grep -c confirmed directly against the full captured log, ~27MB).

Wrote test/specs/REQ-218.md with the full AC-to-test mapping, the gap-check reasoning, the 3-bug account, and both verification-run transcripts.
result.next_action: Route to TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR to independently confirm the AC3 two-sub-clause gap analysis, the new test's determinism argument, and re-run the suite for flakiness.
